**Test image observations:**
- Tomato leaf that is mostly green but with significant **brown necrotic margins** (edges and tip)
- Interior of leaf is still green — necrosis is progressing inward from margins
- No discrete circular spots with concentric rings
- No powdery coating, no webbing, no yellowing/mosaic pattern
- Leaf appears slightly distorted/curled

**Key differential:** The marginal necrosis pattern — brown dead tissue at the leaf edges extending inward — is the hallmark of **Verticillium Wilt**, which produces "V-shaped lesions extending inward from leaf margins" with brown necrotic tissue developing within those lesions.

The Target_Spot reference shows small scattered brown pinpoint spots with concentric rings across the leaf surface — that does not match this image.

```json
{"prediction": "Verticillium_Wilt", "confidence": 0.72, "reasoning": "The leaf shows characteristic marginal necrosis — brown dead tissue at the leaf edges and tip extending inward — with the interior still green. This matches the Verticillium Wilt description of V-shaped lesions extending inward from leaf margins with brown necrotic tissue, on an otherwise still-green leaf. No concentric ring spots (Early Blight, Target Spot), no powdery coating (Powdery Mildew), no webbing (Spider Mites), and no mosaic/curl pattern (viral diseases)."}
```
